750H: Evac+Chair Emergency Stair Chair with 500 lb Capacity
Product URL: https://www.anchortex.com/products/evac-chair-750h-evacuation-stair-chair
Manufacturer page: https://evac-chair.com/evacuation-chairs/evacchair-750h/
Spec sheets: 750H data sheet, Evac+Chair range brochure
Keywords (Ricky's sheet): Primary: emergency stair chair (90/mo, KD1). Secondary: evac chair 750h (0, not indexed). Ricky's note: confirm the 750H capacity with Andrew before using bariatric or heavy duty terms: the product copy does not say, and heavy duty / high capacity evacuation chair both show 0 volume.
Recommended H1 and Subtitle
H1: Evac+Chair Emergency Stair Chair with 500 lb Capacity and Carry Handles – 750H
Current H1: Evac+Chair 750H Evacuation Stair Chair
Subtitle: Robust Aluminum Evacuation Chair with Self-Braking Tracks for One-Person Descent and Carry Handles for Taking a Passenger Up the Stairs
Current subtitle: Evac+Chair 750H Evacuation Stair Chair
Revised Product Description
Headings marked [H2] should be set as H2 on the page.
The Evac+Chair 750H is an emergency stair chair built for strength, with a high strength aluminum frame and a 500 lb weight capacity, the highest of Evac+Chair’s manual evacuation chairs. One operator can take a passenger down the stairs, and the chair has carry handles and additional operator handles so it can also be carried up the stairs.
Adjustable, self-braking Evac+Trac tracks control the speed of descent, so a small operator can move a passenger up to three times their size with no heavy lifting. A padded head support and a quick release 4-point harness hold the passenger securely, and wipeable materials with anti-microbial paint help with infection control. The chair opens in seconds and folds for wall mounting near the stairwell.
Frame: High strength aluminum frame for strength and continued use
Tracks: Adjustable self-braking Evac+Trac tracks control the speed of descent
Handles: Anti-slip, height adjustable main handle; additional operator handles for added stability and for carrying the chair up the stairs
Head Support: Headrest with a padded cushion
Harness: Quick release 4-point passenger harness
Wheels: Industrial locking rear wheels keep the chair still when needed
Visibility: Reflective decals help people find the chair in an emergency
Infection Control: Wipeable materials and anti-microbial paint
Operation: One or two operators; one-person operation going down the stairs
Stairs: Straight staircases (not spiral), at least 23” wide, with a 20° to 40° angle; down, or up by carrying
Weight Capacity: 500 lbs
Weight: 41 lbs
Folded Size: 22.4”W×10.4”D×43.3”H
Certifications: FDA registered; CE marked; ISO 13485 certified
Includes: 4-point passenger harness, cushioned head support, photoluminescent signage, wall hooks, dust cover, and user guide
Warranty: Lifetime manufacturer’s warranty
Available Models and Options
750H – Emergency Stair Chair: Aluminum frame, one- or two-person operation, 500 lb capacity, 41 lbs
[H2] Applications
The 750H suits buildings that need a strong evacuation chair for heavier passengers, frequent use, or carrying a passenger up as well as down the stairs.
Typical applications include:
Hospitals, clinics, and care facilities, where wipeable surfaces help with infection control
Offices, hotels, and high-rise buildings
Schools, universities, and public buildings
Explore Anchortex's Evacuation Chairs and Stretchers collection for more evacuation equipment.
[H2] Frequently Asked Questions
What is an emergency stair chair?
An emergency stair chair is a folding chair with tracks that lets an operator move a person with limited mobility down the stairs when the elevators cannot be used. The Evac+Chair 750H does this with self-braking tracks, so the operator guides the chair instead of carrying the passenger.
What is the weight capacity of the 750H?
The 750H holds passengers up to 500 lbs, and the chair itself weighs 41 lbs.
Can the 750H go up the stairs?
Yes, by carrying. It has carry handles and additional operator handles so the chair can be carried up the stairs. Going down, one operator guides it on its self-braking tracks.
How is the 750H different from the 400H?
The 750H has a high strength aluminum frame, a higher weight capacity (500 lbs instead of 440 lbs), and carry handles for going up the stairs. The 400H is lighter (30 lbs) and has a dual-position seat, armrests, and a footrest, but it only goes down the stairs.
[H2] About Evac+Chair Evacuation Chairs
Evac+Chair makes stair evacuation chairs, powered stair chairs, evacuation sleds, and accessories for moving people with limited mobility on stairs, in an emergency or every day.
The Evac+Chair line includes:
Emergency evacuation chairs: The 300H, 400H, 600H, and 750H stair evacuation chairs for controlled travel down the stairs
Powered stair climbing chairs: The battery powered Power 800 and Power 900 for going up and down the stairs
Stair transport seat: The IBEX 700H Tran-Seat for two-person transport up and down the stairs
Evacuation sleds and mats: The Evac+Sled, Ulti-Mat, and Evac+Sheet rescue sheet
Accessories: Comfy Seat, transfer seat, storage cabinets, anti-theft alarms, and the iEvac smoke and fire escape hood
[H2] About Evac+Chair
Evac+Chair has made stairway evacuation chairs since 1982, and its chairs were designed in the United States. Explore the full line of Evac+Chair evacuation chairs at Anchortex.

Notes and Questions
Keywords: the primary keyword "emergency stair chair" is in the H1, first sentence, an FAQ, the meta title, and the meta description. "Evac chair 750h" is covered by "Evac+Chair 750H" in the meta title and body.
Capacity (Ricky asked to confirm this with you): the 750H data sheet (VERS 2/750/7-24), the Evac+Chair web page, and our current page say 500 lbs; the Evac+Chair range brochure says 440 lbs. I used 500 lbs (data sheet). As Ricky suggested, I did not use "bariatric" or "heavy duty" (both show 0 volume). Is 500 lbs right, and would you like either term on the page?
Warranty: the data sheet and brochure say "Lifetime Warranty"; the web page and our current page say "Manufacturer's Warranty." I used lifetime (data sheet).
Stairs: the data sheet text says the tracks work "on all types of stairways," but its staircase icon shows straight stairs only, with spiral stairs crossed out. I used straight stairs only. Is that right?
Upward: the data sheet says the carry handles let the chair be carried upstairs, and its icons show travel both up and down. It does not say how many people are needed to carry it up, so I did not give a number.
Name: the Evac+Chair web page has a button that says "Find out more about the Power 750H," but the 750H is a manual chair with no motor, like the 400H. I did not use "Power."
Price: $2,350 with no compare-at price. The other Evac+Chair pages have a compare-at price (price = 75%). Should the 750H have one?
Left out: "World's No.1," "beware of poor imitations," 9/11, "ultimate control," and "exceeds fire safety requirements ... Americans with Disabilities Act."
Duplicate content: our current description is the Evac+Chair web page text word for word, plus an old "About Evac+Chair of North America" paragraph. The new copy is fully rewritten.
Images: the 2 current images are kept (stairwell photo 1024×893 and numbered features diagram 1024×874). Evac+Chair has the same two at larger sizes (2560×2231 and 2480×2116) but no other photos. Would you like the larger versions?
Shipping weight: the variant is set to 200 lbs; the chair weighs 41 lbs. Is 200 lbs a placeholder, as on the other Evac+Chair pages?
Current meta description is the general GSA pricing line. GSA is not mentioned in the description, per your note on the other tabs.
